title: Scheidbare werkwoorden (separable verbs)
summary: Separable verbs = prefix + main verb. The prefix splits off and goes to the end of the sentence in main clauses.
rules: A separable verb is a prefix (e.g. uit-, op-, in-, aan-, af-, mee-, voor-, door-, terug-) + main verb. The prefix changes the meaning.
Rule 1 — only verb in the sentence: separate. Move the prefix to the end. Hij nodigt mijn vriend uit.
Rule 2 — combined with a modal/auxiliary (kunnen, mogen, moeten, willen, zullen, hoeven, gaan): keep together as infinitive at end. Ik wil hem uitnodigen.
In perfectum, the past participle keeps the prefix and inserts -ge- between prefix and stem: aangekleed, meegenomen, opgeschreven, ingestapt.
In subclauses all verbs go to the end and the separable verb stays together (or follows the V2 rules of the subclause).
Exception: prefixes her-, ge-, be-, ont-, ver- are NOT separable. Stress test: if stress is on the prefix → separable.
With reflexive verbs the reflexive pronoun follows the verb, prefix still goes to end.
